motions.headline: Recycling use sent back for a rewrite
motions.summary: The council turned down changes to zoning definitions, conditional uses and land use tables, and asked staff to return with the recycling piece as a special use.
motions.impact: Nothing in the zoning code changed today. The recycling part comes back to the council later as a special use; the rest of the proposal is off the table.

motions.item_title: Approve an ordinance of Eagle Mountain Ci'tg, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an ordinance of Eagle Mountain Ci'tg, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.60.120 General Fencing Prouisions changing the last sentence to state, "Fence or wall height Is measured or assessed from either: a) ne height of finished grade of the property whereupon a fence lies or to which It pertains, to the top of the fence or wall; or, b) from the height of the grade of a commercial or Industrial building/parking pad where such Is at a higher grade eleuation than any abutting residentially zoned or developed property - whichever results in a higher screen." Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Taller fences where businesses sit above homes
motions.summary: Fence height gets measured differently now: where a commercial or industrial pad sits above neighboring homes, the council set the taller screen as the standard.
motions.impact: If a business lot beside your yard is built up higher than your property, the screening fence is measured from that higher pad and blocks more. Only homes on those boundaries, and the builders next door, are touched.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain Citg, Utah, to Repeal and Replace Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.16 Citg Administrator Councilmember Wood reviewed the changes requested bg the Citg Council during work session provided in an email sent bg the Citg Attorneg. Discussion determined to add the option for the Citg Council to table the establishment of the recruitment process to account for circumstances in which the Citg is unable to move forward with the process at the next regularlg scheduled meeting following ang vacancg.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, to Repeal and Replace Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.16 City Administrator with the changes provided by the City Attorney to 2.16 City Manager as follows: l. 2.16.020 Paragraph 2, oFor any vacancy of the position of City Manager, the City Council, with the Mayor as a voting member, may appoint an acting City Manager to Immediately assume the duties and responsibilities of the City Manager and conduct the day-to-day operations and business of the city during any Interim period. This Individual may or may not be someone that Is In consideration for the position of City Manager;" 2. 2.16.020 Paragraph 3, "Unless the urgencg of the situation reguhes an earlier special meeting, the City Council shall establish the recruitment process, scope of responsibilities, salary and benefits offered for the City Manager position during the next regularlg scheduled meeting following any vacancy. Notwithstanding the the City Council may table the matter in Its discretion. Unless the City Council otherwise directs, the City Attorney and the Human Resource Manager shall secure a minimum of three executive recruitment firms that specialize In municipal government for candidate searches. lf the City Council decides to hire a recruitment firm, the City Council shall Interuiew a minimum of three firms;" and 3. 2.16.020 Paragraph 4, "The candidates shall be evaluated by the City Council as prouided by the recruiting firm. Existing staff that desire to be considered for the position will submit their application to the recruiting firm. lf the recruiting firm finds that the Indiuidual meets the criteria for the position, they will be added to the candidates for consideration by the City Council. The recruiting firm will provide the City Council with the application materials of all candidates and recommend their top five choices. The City Council shall not be bound by the recommendation and shall choose which candidates to interuiew. All Interuiews by the City Council shall be conducted in a closed seEsion." Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for hiring a city manager
motions.summary: The city rewrote the code covering its top appointed job, renaming it city manager and setting how a vacancy is filled and candidates recruited.
motions.impact: Candidate interviews stay closed to the public, so when the job next opens you will see the appointment rather than the choosing. Nothing about city services changes.

motions.item_title: Adopt the legislative priorities list as presented during the meeting with the addition of the…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt the legislative priorities list as presented during the meeting with the addition of the match grant program as a proposed item for future consideration. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City's asks of the state legislature set
motions.summary: The council adopted its list of priorities to push at the state legislature, adding a matching grant program to be taken up later.
motions.impact: This one shapes what the city asks lawmakers for, nothing more. No resident feels it.
